Photoreal live-action, London, March 1881, low raking lamplight, deep black shadow, 35 mm film grain.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:08. The shot begins from <Picture 1>: an insert on two narrow wheel ruts pressed deep in the mud of the roadway at the kerb, grey water standing in them, the edge of the brick kerbstone at the top of frame; only what <Picture 1> shows is in frame. The camera is over the roadway at the height of a stooping man's eye, an arm's length from the ruts, a 90mm lens. The grey light comes from the LEFT along the ruts. At the first frame the two narrow ruts run from the BOTTOM edge up the CENTRE of the frame a hand's width apart with grey water in them. The kerbstone crosses the TOP third and the ruts' far walls are black. The camera pans right along the kerb across the whole shot, travelling a finger's breadth as the two ruts keep the frame's centre, from 00:00 to 00:03. At 00:03 a drop falls into the water in one rut. At 00:05 the ripple spreads a finger's breadth, and the movement continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:08 the camera is panning right through the last frame, and the action continues with it.
